ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: Descended from Austronesian seafarers of the Lapita culture, they reached Tonga and Samoa around 800 BCE and later found the remotest islands by stars, winds and swells.
A line of sacred kings at Muʻa on Tongatapu whose voyaging and tribute networks reached ʻUvea, Samoa and eastern Fiji.
The first rulers of all Pohnpei governed from Nan Madol, nearly a hundred artificial islets of stacked basalt in a coral lagoon.
Settled around 1200 on one of the remotest inhabited islands on Earth, its people carved some 887 moai and devised rongorongo, the only possible script known from Polynesia.
The Raiatean priest and navigator who joined Cook's Endeavour in 1769, drew a chart of the islands Tahitians knew and spoke for Cook with the Māori.
Three voyages between 1768 and 1779 charted New Zealand and eastern Australia; the last ended with his death in a clash at Kealakekua Bay on Hawaii Island.
United by Kamehameha I by 1810 and recognised by Britain and France in 1843, it was overthrown in 1893 by businessmen backed by US troops.
Signed in 1840 by the British Crown and Māori chiefs, in English and Māori texts that differ on sovereignty: a dispute the Waitangi Tribunal has heard since 1975.
The only Pacific island state never formally colonised: the kingdom George Tupou I founded in 1845, whose constitution of 1875 is still in force.
